The Big Short: It's Surprisingly Entertaining AND Educational

If you lived through the crash of '08 this might be especially interesting but holy shit for some reason a movie about stock market bullshit became fascinating for me to watch.

One of the things they do are these 4th Wall Breaks (risky but here it works perfectly) but the narrator is describing some bullshit complex sounding financial thing like 'shorting' or 'CDOs' or whatnot and "Heres Selena Gomez to explain what this is". Gomez gives an analogy the average person can grasp. the thing is - you can totally get it. By the end of the movie you really can totally understand all this 'mortgage bubble' nonsense and what was going on. BTW: I was always under some impression the guys 'betting against' were the assholes but in fact no they were not (well, not really). In a sense they were the ones 'calling bullshit'.

2 of the other major angles weren't involved in this story:

  • That in a rare case of bipartisanship it really was a case where Democrats and plenty of Republicans - and with possibly great intentions - agreed they wanted to see 'everyone owning a home'. While its true that Bush Jr and a some major White House people DID warn, sound alarms the truth is they didn't do it often enough or even very loudly. Even though it sounds great and who's going to oppose getting every American into home-ownership (dems or GOP people alike) it was actually a horrifying thing. So the movie doesn't really mention that in a lot of ways government was allowing this. giving it the 'Ok' and greenlight.

The other angle only barely mentioned is what we can call the 'Flatscreen TV' issue. I spent 8 hours on a plane back from Amsterdam with a mortgage consultant explaining the 'Flatscreen TV' situation and by the time we landed in the USA Obama was President. The movie does actually make a 'wink' at this between the Stripper with loans against her 5 or 7 houses but also the scene where the only thing missing from the abandoned house is the flatscreen TV hehe.

Anyways, surprised me how much I liked this movie!
